system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",
 "summary": "<3-5 sentences: what happened or is expected, why, how sure>",
 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

{
  "headline": "The ACCELERATE trial of evacetrapib was stopped for futility in ~12,092 high-risk vascular patients, confirming that CETP inhibition does not reduce cardiovascular events despite large HDL-C increases.",
  "summary": "ACCELERATE randomized 12,092–12,095 patients with high-risk vascular disease to evacetrapib 130 mg daily or placebo on top of statin therapy. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina, with 1,670 planned events. After a median follow-up of 1.5 years, an independent DSMB recommended stopping the trial for futility on October 12, 2015, with no safety signal. Phase 2 data showed evacetrapib raised HDL-C by 103% (placebo-adjusted) and lowered LDL-C by 15% (placebo-adjusted, −0.56 mmol/L). The calculator, using the LDL-C reduction and 1.5-year follow-up, predicted only a 5.7% relative risk reduction (HR 0.943) and 22% power to detect it. The observed result was neutral (HR ~1.01). The failure is best explained by the intended biomarker (HDL-C) not being causally protective for coronary disease, consistent with Mendelian randomization evidence. Genetic support for CETP as a target was uncertain (association score 0.736, zero evidence items before the trial cutoff). No off-target harm was detected (no QT prolongation, no clinically relevant blood pressure effect at therapeutic doses).",
